findings.evidence: The transaction samples PostgreSQL time and proves the token is unexpired at line 753, then performs resource locks, Chunk Set/Embedding Set writes and the activation/attempt close without another fresh clock-and-token check before flush/commit.
findings.problem: The fenced finalization path does not revalidate worker_id, lease_version and the unexpired lease at the commit boundary.
findings.harm: A slow finalization transaction can outlive the lease while holding the job row lock and still publish a succeeded activation or superseded outcome from an expired worker, violating the worker-coordination fencing invariant and allowing stale work to become retrieval-visible.
findings.fix: Take a fresh PostgreSQL clock sample and revalidate the unchanged current token immediately before activation/attempt closure and commit; return Fenced so the transaction rolls back all tentative derivation writes when the lease is no longer valid. Add a deterministic clock/lock probe covering expiry during finalization.

report: Standards review: one major implementation defect. The claim is fenced at entry, but the finalization transaction has no commit-boundary lease recheck. The remaining transaction-probe and raw-retention observations are harness-only capabilities and are addressed by the authorized test harness work.
